intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 (DEE45) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the GABRB1 gene.

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 (DEE45) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the GABRB1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we draw attention to the six mutations that all affect subunits of the gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) ionotropic receptor (four in GABRB3, and one each in GABRA1 and GABRB1)
checks.explanation: The paper reports one de novo GABRB1 mutation in an epileptic encephalopathy patient. It does not show that the mutation causes disease, does not say it is heterozygous and does not name DEE45.

paragraphs.text: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 (DEE45) is a severe neurologic disorder with seizures that begin in infancy. Reported patients had infantile spasms with hypsarrhythmia or epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures, along with severe developmental impairment. The disorder has been caused by de novo heterozygous mutations in the GABRB1 gene, which encodes the beta-1 subunit of the GABA-A receptor (Epi4K Consortium et al., 2013; Janve et al., 2016; Burgess et al., 2019).

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 (DEE45) is a severe neurologic disorder with seizures that begin in infancy.
checks.evidence_quote: Both LGS and IS are severe EEs with early onset and developmental delays, although the temporal course and semiology of the seizures are different.
checks.explanation: Paper describes IS/LGS as severe early-onset EEs but does not name DEE45 or state infantile onset for a GABRB1 disorder explicitly.

checks.claim: Reported patients with DEE45 had infantile spasms with hypsarrhythmia or epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified 2 individuals with pathogenic variants in GABA receptor subunit-encoding genes not previously associated with EIMFS, but reported in association with other developmental and epileptic encephalopathies: one case each for GABRA1 and GABRB1.
checks.explanation: Paper supports EIMFS phenotype for GABRB1; infantile spasms with hypsarrhythmia not described for the GABRB1 patient in this paper (table shows no spasms).

paragraphs.text: Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) studied 264 probands with infantile spasms (IS) or Lennox-Gastaut syndrome. One of them, a patient with IS, carried a de novo GABRB1 mutation. To enter the study, patients with IS had to have hypsarrhythmia on EEG and no moderate-to-severe developmental impairment before seizure onset. Janve et al. (2016) noted that this patient had a severe IS phenotype.

paragraphs.text: Burgess et al. (2019) studied a cohort of patients with epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures (EIMFS). It included 1 patient (patient 63) with a de novo GABRB1 variant. In this patient, focal seizures began at 4 months of age. At the time of study, at 2 years of age, the patient had profound to severe developmental impairment and hypotonia and had become seizure-free.

paragraphs.text: Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) performed exome sequencing on 264 trios, each a proband with IS or Lennox-Gastaut syndrome and the parents. They found a de novo mutation in the GABRB1 gene in 1 patient. The mutation was confirmed by Sanger sequencing of the proband and parents. It was 1 of 6 de novo mutations in the cohort that affected GABA-A receptor subunits: 4 in GABRB3 and 1 each in GABRA1 and GABRB1.

checks.evidence_quote: the six mutations that all affect subunits of the gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) ionotropic receptor (four in GABRB3, and one each in GABRA1 and GABRB1)
checks.explanation: The paper states this breakdown of 4 + 1 + 1 directly.

paragraphs.text: Janve et al. (2016) studied the GABRB1 mutation found by Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) in the patient with IS. It was a heterozygous phe246-to-ser (F246S) substitution in transmembrane domain 1, and F246 is invariant across all GABA-A receptor subunits. The authors coexpressed the mutant beta-1 subunit with alpha-1 and gamma-2L subunits in HEK293T cells. When only the mutant beta-1 subunit was expressed, peak GABA-evoked current density fell by a minor 25%. When wildtype and mutant beta-1 were coexpressed, current density did not change. The mutation slowed current deactivation. At the single-channel level, mean open time increased about 3.75-fold and burst duration about 3.2-fold, while opening frequency and conductance (about 21 pS) were reduced. The mutation also increased holding currents about 5-fold, and spontaneous open probability increased 4-fold, indicating spontaneous channel openings. Surface levels of the mutant subunit were slightly but significantly reduced, while total levels were unchanged. Janve et al. (2016) concluded that the mutation impaired GABA-A receptor function, chiefly by altering current kinetics.

checks.claim: The GABRB1 mutation found by Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) in the patient with infantile spasms was a heterozygous F246S substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: Since the LGS and IS patients were heterozygous for the de novo GABRB3 and GABRB1 mutations
checks.explanation: Combined with 'one IS patient had a mutation in the GABAA receptor β1 subunit gene (GABRB1(F246S))'.

checks.claim: The GABRB1 F246S substitution is located in transmembrane domain 1.
checks.evidence_quote: transmembrane domain 1 (TM1, F246)

checks.claim: GABRB1 residue F246 is invariant across all GABA-A receptor subunits.
checks.evidence_quote: we found that D120, Y302 and F246 are invariant residues across all GABAA receptor subunits.

checks.claim: Janve et al. (2016) coexpressed the GABRB1 F246S mutant beta-1 subunit with alpha-1 and gamma-2L subunits in HEK293T cells.
checks.evidence_quote: GABAA receptor α1 and γ2L subunits were coexpressed with wild-type and/or mutant β3 or β1 subunits in HEK 293T cells.

checks.claim: When only the GABRB1 F246S mutant beta-1 subunit was expressed, peak GABA-evoked current density fell by a minor 25%.
checks.evidence_quote: Under similar hom expression conditions, current densities from cells expressing β1(F246S) subunits had a minor (25%) reduction of peak current densities

checks.claim: When wildtype and GABRB1 F246S mutant beta-1 subunits were coexpressed, peak GABA-evoked current density did not change.
checks.evidence_quote: The β1(F246S) subunit mutation also had no effects on current density in the het condition

checks.claim: The GABRB1 F246S mutation slowed GABA-A receptor current deactivation.
checks.evidence_quote: In contrast to the β3 mutations, the β1(F246S) subunit mutation reduced the deactivation rate (increased weighted deactivation rate constant) compared to wt currents

checks.claim: The GABRB1 F246S mutation increased single-channel mean open time about 3.75-fold.
checks.evidence_quote: a gain of function resulted in increased mean open time (~3.75 fold) and burst duration (~3.2 fold) from prolonged openings.

checks.claim: The GABRB1 F246S mutation increased single-channel burst duration about 3.2-fold.
checks.evidence_quote: a gain of function resulted in increased mean open time (~3.75 fold) and burst duration (~3.2 fold) from prolonged openings.

checks.claim: The GABRB1 F246S mutation reduced single-channel opening frequency.
checks.evidence_quote: the IS-associated β1(F246S) subunit mutation did not alter channel Po despite decreasing opening frequency.

checks.claim: The GABRB1 F246S mutation reduced single-channel conductance (to about 21 pS).
checks.evidence_quote: Furthermore, reduced conductance level of ~21 pS accounted for a small reduction of whole cell GABA-evoked currents in the β1(F246S) hom condition.

checks.claim: The GABRB1 F246S mutation increased holding currents about 5-fold.
checks.evidence_quote: Both LGS-associated GABRB3(E180G) and IS-associated GABRB1(F246S) mutations significantly increased (~5 fold) holding currents recorded from α1βγ2L receptors, suggesting spontaneous channel openings in hom, but not het, conditions

checks.claim: The GABRB1 F246S mutation increased spontaneous open probability 4-fold, indicating spontaneous channel openings.
checks.evidence_quote: GABAA receptors containing the β1(F246S) subunit mutation increased spontaneous Po by 4-fold (Figure 8F, right panel) but did not alter single-channel conductance.

checks.claim: Surface levels of the GABRB1 F246S mutant subunit were slightly but significantly reduced.
checks.evidence_quote: The β1(F246S)HA subunit expression levels were slightly, but significantly, reduced compared to wt β1HA levels

checks.claim: Total levels of the GABRB1 F246S mutant subunit were unchanged.
checks.evidence_quote: Total expression levels of α1, β1HA or γ2LHA were not changed (Figure 4E).

checks.claim: Janve et al. (2016) concluded that the GABRB1 F246S mutation impaired GABA-A receptor function, chiefly by altering current kinetics.
checks.evidence_quote: All 5 de novo GABRB mutations impaired GABAA receptor function by rearranging conserved structural domains, supporting their role in EEs. The primary effect of LGS-associated mutations was reduced GABA-evoked peak current amplitudes, whereas the major impact of IS-associated mutations was on current kinetic properties.

paragraphs.text: In a patient with EIMFS (patient 63), Burgess et al. (2019) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a de novo heterozygous variant in the GABRB1 gene, an ile247-to-thr (I247T) substitution (chr4:47405633T-C, GRCh37). The variant was absent from the ExAC and gnomAD databases. SIFT predicted it to be deleterious and PolyPhen predicted it to be benign. The authors classified it as likely pathogenic.

paragraphs.text: Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) found a de novo heterozygous GABRB1 mutation in a patient with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 (DEE45) who had infantile spasms. The mutation was identified by trio exome sequencing and confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Janve et al. (2016) identified the mutation as a phe246-to-ser (F246S) substitution at an invariant residue in transmembrane domain 1. In HEK293T cells, the mutant subunit caused a minor (25%) reduction in peak GABA-evoked current when expressed alone and no reduction when coexpressed with wildtype. It slowed current deactivation, increased single-channel mean open time (about 3.75-fold) and burst duration (about 3.2-fold), and increased spontaneous channel open probability 4-fold.
